cond_0001.intro: This job evaluates, initiates, and maintains all activities related to the conduct of clinical trials. Communicates with external funding agencies and sponsors, other departments, departmental staff, and patients to ensure the understanding of the requirements of conducting and participating in clinical trials. Organizes and manages all patient care requirements. Coordinates trials that are more complex and/or a greater number of trials than the associate level.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Organizes strategies for recruiting study participants and screening study participants for eligibility on the telephone, in the clinic, and other settings as required. Coordinates and oversees patient (study participant) activity as it relates to the conduct of research and clinical trials, serving as a liaison for both patient and Principal Investigator (PI). Serves as primary point of contact for patient to report and triage adverse events and independently conducts informed consent. Arranges necessary tests and procedures in accordance with protocol requirements and reports results to the investigator. Performs clinical laboratory activities as required per protocol and maintains study supplies and equipment. Maintains close communication with study sponsor representatives including but not limited to site initiation, maintenance, and close out of studies. Develops and maintains all required documentation as it relates to the conduct of assigned clinical trials and associated patient care. Completes data entry into sponsor-specific data entry systems and/or supports data coordinator, including query resolution and transcribes information across various internal and external electronic data systems. Conducts daily work and clinical trial activity in accordance with Good Clinical Practice Guidelines. Adapts behavior to the specific patient population, including but not limited to respect for privacy, method of introduction to the patient, adapting explanation of services or procedures to be performed, requesting permissions and communication style. Performs other related duties as assigned.
The above statements describe the general nature and level of work only. They are not an exhaustive list of all required responsibilities, duties, and skills. Other duties may be added, or this description amended at any time.
Remains knowledgeable on current federal, state, and local laws, accreditation standards or regulatory agency requirements that apply to the assigned area of responsibility and ensures compliance with all such laws, regulations, and standards.
This employer maintains and complies with its Compliance & Privacy Program and Standards of Conduct, including the immediate reporting of any known or suspected unethical or questionable behaviors or conduct; patient/employee safety, patient privacy, and/or other compliance-related concerns.
Physical and Environmental Demands
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Medium Work - Exerting 20 to 50 pounds of force occasionally, and/or 10 to 25 pounds of force frequently, and/or greater than negligible up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects. (Constantly: activity or condition exists 2/3 or more of the time) to move objects. Physical demand requirements are in excess of those for Sedentary Work. Even though the weight lifted may be only a negligible amount, a job should be rated Light Work: (1) when it requires walking or standing to a significant degree; or (2) when it requires sitting most of the time but entails pushing and/or pulling of arm or leg controls; and/or (3) when the job requires working at a production rate pace entailing the constant pushing and/or pulling of materials even though the weight of those materials is negligible. NOTE: The constant stress and strain of maintaining a production rate pace, especially in an industrial setting, can be and is physically demanding of a worker even though the amount of force exerted is negligible.
Duties performed routinely require exposure to blood, body fluid and tissue.
The incumbent works in a patient care area; works in an area where patients enter; works directly with patients; and/or works with specimens that could contain communicable diseases. The incumbent has an occupational risk for exposure to all communicable diseases.
Because the incumbent works within a healthcare setting, there may be occupational risk for exposure to hazardous medications or hazardous waste within the environment through receipt, transport, storage, preparation, dispensing, administration, cleaning and/or disposal of contaminated waste. The risk level of exposure may increase depending on the essential job duties of the role.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent
3 Years of relevant research experience in a clinical setting, OR 2 years of relevant research experience in a clinical setting with ACRP or SOCRA certification
Current Basic Life Support (BLS) certification from the American Heart Association within 60 days of hire. Exceptions will be granted for those in fully remote status
Knowledge of medical and clinical research terminology and processes
Working knowledge of ICH guidelines for ethical conduct of research
Working knowledge of the requirements and regulations associated with the conduct of clinical trials and other related research activity
Strong critical thinking skills
Effective verbal and written communication skills and ability to present information clearly and professionally to varying levels of individuals throughout the patient care process
Strong organizational and time management skills and ability to multi-task, pay close attention to detail, and learn new techniques
Ability to travel throughout and between facilities and work a flexible work schedule, including on-call, weekend, and night shifts
Preferred Requirements
Ability to follow and provide critical feedback on the investigational plan
Ability to develop study related budgets, contracts, and patient consent documents
Proficiency in using computers, software, and web-based applications, including working knowledge of [Product name masked]

The role organizes and manages all patient care requirements and coordinates trials that are more complex and/or greater in number than the associate level.
cond_0042.responsibilities:
Organizes strategies for recruiting study participants and actively screens them for eligibility on the telephone, in the clinic, and other settings as required.
Coordinates and oversees patient (study participant) activity as it relates to the conduct of research and clinical trials, serving as a liaison between the patient and Principal Investigator (PI).
Serves as the primary point of contact for patients to report and triage adverse events, and independently conducts informed consent.
Arranges necessary tests and procedures in accordance with protocol requirements and communicates results directly to the investigator.
Performs clinical laboratory activities as required per protocol and maintains study supplies and equipment.
Maintains regular, ongoing communication with study sponsor representatives including site initiation, maintenance, and close out of studies.
Develops and maintains all required documentation related to the conduct of assigned clinical trials and associated patient care.
Completes data entry into sponsor-specific data entry systems and/or supports the data coordinator, including query resolution, and transcribes information across various internal and external electronic data systems.
Conducts daily work and clinical trial activity in accordance with Good Clinical Practice Guidelines.
Adapts behavior to the specific patient population, including respect for privacy, method of introduction to the patient, adapting explanation of services or procedures to be performed, requesting permissions, and communication style.
Remains knowledgeable on current federal, state, and local laws, accreditation standards, and regulatory agency requirements that apply to the assigned area of responsibility and ensures compliance with all such laws, regulations, and standards.
Complies with [Company name masked]'s Compliance & Privacy Program and Standards of Conduct, including the immediate reporting of any known or suspected unethical or questionable behaviors or conduct; patient/employee safety, patient privacy, and/or other compliance-related concerns.
Performs other related duties as assigned.
The above statements describe the general nature and level of work only. They are not an exhaustive list of all required responsibilities, duties, and skills. Other duties may be added, or this description amended at any time.
cond_0042.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent
3 Years of relevant research experience in a clinical setting, OR 2 years of relevant research experience in a clinical setting with ACRP or SOCRA certification
Current Basic Life Support (BLS) certification from the American Heart Association within 60 days of hire (exceptions granted for those in fully remote status)
Knowledge of medical and clinical research terminology and processes
Working knowledge of ICH guidelines for ethical conduct of research
Working knowledge of the requirements and regulations associated with the conduct of clinical trials and other related research activity
Effective verbal and written communication skills and ability to present information clearly and professionally to varying levels of individuals throughout the patient care process
Ability to follow and provide critical feedback on the investigational plan
Ability to travel throughout and between facilities and work a flexible work schedule, including on-call, weekend, and night shifts
Preferred Requirements
Strong critical thinking skills
Ability to develop study-related budgets, contracts, and patient consent documents
Proficiency in using computers, software, and web-based applications, including working knowledge of [Product name masked]
Strong organizational and time management skills and ability to multi-task, pay close attention to detail, and learn new techniques
Physical and Environmental Demands
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Medium Work - Exerting 20 to 50 pounds of force occasionally, and/or 10 to 25 pounds of force frequently, and/or greater than negligible up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects. (Constantly: activity or condition exists 2/3 or more of the time) to move objects. Physical demand requirements are in excess of those for Sedentary Work. Even though the weight lifted may be only a negligible amount, a job should be rated Light Work: (1) when it requires walking or standing to a significant degree; or (2) when it requires sitting most of the time but entails pushing and/or pulling of arm or leg controls; and/or (3) when the job requires working at a production rate pace entailing the constant pushing and/or pulling of materials even though the weight of those materials is negligible. NOTE: The constant stress and strain of maintaining a production rate pace, especially in an industrial setting, can be and is physically demanding of a worker even though the amount of force exerted is negligible.
Duties performed routinely require exposure to blood, body fluid and tissue.
The incumbent works in a patient care area; works in an area where patients enter; works directly with patients; and/or works with specimens that could contain communicable diseases. The incumbent has an occupational risk for exposure to all communicable diseases.
Because the incumbent works within a healthcare setting, there may be occupational risk for exposure to hazardous medications or hazardous waste within the environment through receipt, transport, storage, preparation, dispensing, administration, cleaning and/or disposal of contaminated waste. You will take direct responsibility for communicating with external funding agencies and sponsors, other departments, departmental staff, and patients to ensure the requirements of conducting and participating in clinical trials are met. You will manage all patient care requirements and lead trials that are more complex and/or greater in number than the associate level.
cond_0071.responsibilities:
Lead strategies for recruiting study participants and screening them for eligibility on the telephone, in the clinic, and other settings as required.
Direct and oversee patient (study participant) activity as it relates to the conduct of research and clinical trials, serving as a liaison for both patient and Principal Investigator (PI).
Serve as primary point of contact for patients to report and triage adverse events and independently conduct informed consent.
Arrange necessary tests and procedures in accordance with protocol requirements and report results to the investigator.
Execute clinical laboratory activities as required per protocol and maintain study supplies and equipment.
Drive close communication with study sponsor representatives including but not limited to site initiation, maintenance, and close out of studies.
Develop and maintain all required documentation as it relates to the conduct of assigned clinical trials and associated patient care.
Own data entry into sponsor-specific data entry systems and/or direct data coordinator support, including query resolution, and transcribe information across various internal and external electronic data systems.
Conduct daily work and clinical trial activity in accordance with Good Clinical Practice Guidelines.
Adapt behavior to the specific patient population, including but not limited to respect for privacy, method of introduction to the patient, adapting explanation of services or procedures to be performed, requesting permissions and communication style.
Perform other related duties as assigned.
Remain knowledgeable on current federal, state, and local laws, accreditation standards or regulatory agency requirements that apply to the assigned area of responsibility and ensure compliance with all such laws, regulations, and standards.
Maintain and comply with the Compliance & Privacy Program and Standards of Conduct, including the immediate reporting of any known or suspected unethical or questionable behaviors or conduct; patient/employee safety, patient privacy, and/or other compliance-related concerns.
cond_0071.requirements:
High school diploma or equivalent.
3 Years of relevant research experience in a clinical setting,
OR
2 Years of relevant research experience in a clinical setting with ACRP or SOCRA certification.
Current Basic Life Support (BLS) certification from the American Heart Association within 60 days of hire. Exceptions will be granted for those in fully remote status.
Knowledge of medical and clinical research terminology and processes. Working knowledge of ICH guidelines for ethical conduct of research. Strong critical thinking skills. Ability to follow and provide critical feedback on the investigational plan. Ability to develop study related budgets, contracts, and patient consent documents. Working knowledge of the requirements and regulations associated with the conduct of clinical trials and other related research activity. Proficiency in using computers, software, and web-based applications, including working knowledge of [Product name masked]. Effective verbal and written communication skills and ability to present information clearly and professionally to varying levels of individuals throughout the patient care process. Strong organizational and time management skills and ability to multi-task, pay close attention to detail, and learn new techniques. Ability to travel throughout and between facilities and work a flexible work schedule, including on-call, weekend, and night shifts.
Physical and Environmental Demands:
Medium Work - Exerting 20 to 50 pounds of force occasionally, and/or 10 to 25 pounds of force frequently, and/or greater than negligible up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects. (Constantly: activity or condition exists 2/3 or more of the time) to move objects. Physical demand requirements are in excess of those for Sedentary Work. Even though the weight lifted may be only a negligible amount, a job should be rated Light Work: (1) when it requires walking or standing to a significant degree; or (2) when it requires sitting most of the time but entails pushing and/or pulling of arm or leg controls; and/or (3) when the job requires working at a production rate pace entailing the constant pushing and/or pulling of materials even though the weight of those materials is negligible. NOTE: The constant stress and strain of maintaining a production rate pace, especially in an industrial setting, can be and is physically demanding of a worker even though the amount of force exerted is negligible.
Duties performed routinely require exposure to blood, body fluid and tissue.
The incumbent works in a patient care area; works in an area where patients enter; works directly with patients; and/or works with specimens that could contain communicable diseases. The incumbent has an occupational risk for exposure to all communicable diseases.
Because the incumbent works within a healthcare setting, there may be occupational risk for exposure to hazardous medications or hazardous waste within the environment through receipt, transport, storage, preparation, dispensing, administration, cleaning and/or disposal of contaminated waste. The risk level of exposure may increase depending on the essential job duties of the role.

cond_0133.intro: This role evaluates, initiates, and maintains all activities related to the conduct of clinical trials. It involves coordinating with external funding agencies and sponsors, other departments, departmental staff, and patients to ensure requirements for conducting and participating in clinical trials are understood and met. Organizes and manages all patient care requirements. Coordinates trials that are more complex and/or greater in number than the associate level.
cond_0133.responsibilities:
Organizes strategies for recruiting study participants and screens them for eligibility by telephone, in the clinic, and other settings as required.
Coordinates and oversees patient (study participant) activity as it relates to the conduct of research and clinical trials, serving as a liaison between the patient and Principal Investigator (PI).
Serves as primary point of contact for patients to report and triage adverse events and independently conducts informed consent.
Arranges necessary tests and procedures in accordance with protocol requirements and reports results to the investigator.
Performs clinical laboratory activities as required per protocol and maintains study supplies and equipment.
Coordinates with study sponsor representatives on site initiation, maintenance, and close out of studies.
Develops and maintains all required documentation related to assigned clinical trials and associated patient care.
Completes data entry into sponsor-specific systems and/or supports the data coordinator, including query resolution, and transcribes information across various internal and external electronic data systems.
Conducts daily work and clinical trial activity in accordance with Good Clinical Practice Guidelines.
Adapts approach to the specific patient population, including respect for privacy, method of introduction, explanation of services or procedures, requesting permissions, and communication style.
Remains knowledgeable on current federal, state, and local laws, accreditation standards, and regulatory agency requirements applicable to the assigned area and ensures compliance.
Complies with the organization's Compliance & Privacy Program and Standards of Conduct, including immediate reporting of any known or suspected unethical or questionable behaviors; patient/employee safety, patient privacy, and/or other compliance-related concerns.
Performs other related duties as assigned.
The above statements describe the general nature and level of work only. They are not an exhaustive list of all required responsibilities, duties, and skills. Other duties may be added, or this description amended at any time.
Physical and Environmental Demands:
Medium Work - Exerting 20 to 50 pounds of force occasionally, and/or 10 to 25 pounds of force frequently, and/or greater than negligible up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects.
Duties performed routinely require exposure to blood, body fluid, and tissue.
The incumbent works in a patient care area; works in an area where patients enter; works directly with patients; and/or works with specimens that could contain communicable diseases. The incumbent has an occupational risk for exposure to all communicable diseases.
Because the incumbent works within a healthcare setting, there may be occupational risk for exposure to hazardous medications or hazardous waste within the environment through receipt, transport, storage, preparation, dispensing, administration, cleaning and/or disposal of contaminated waste. The risk level of exposure may increase depending on the essential job duties of the role.
cond_0133.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent
3 Years of relevant research experience in a clinical setting, OR 2 years of relevant research experience in a clinical setting with ACRP or SOCRA certification
Current Basic Life Support (BLS) certification from the American Heart Association within 60 days of hire (exceptions granted for fully remote status)
Knowledge of medical and clinical research terminology and processes
Working knowledge of ICH guidelines for ethical conduct of research
Working knowledge of the requirements and regulations associated with the conduct of clinical trials and other related research activity
Strong critical thinking skills
Ability to follow and provide critical feedback on the investigational plan
Strong written communication and clear, direct verbal reporting skills
Strong organizational and time management skills; ability to multi-task, pay close attention to detail, and learn new techniques
Preferred Requirements
Ability to develop study-related budgets, contracts, and patient consent documents
Proficiency in using computers, software, and web-based applications, including working knowledge of [Product name masked]
Ability to travel throughout and between facilities and work a flexible schedule, including on-call, weekend, and night shifts

High school diploma or equivalent.
3 Years of relevant research experience in a clinical setting, OR 2 years of relevant research experience in a clinical setting with ACRP or SOCRA certification.

Working knowledge of ICH guidelines for ethical conduct of research.

Strong critical thinking skills.
Ability to follow and provide critical feedback on the investigational plan.
Ability to develop study related budgets, contracts, and patient consent documents.
Proficiency in using computers, software, and web-based applications, including working knowledge of [Product name masked].
Strong organizational and time management skills and ability to multi-task, pay close attention to detail, and learn new techniques.

cond_0262.intro: We are looking for a Clinical Research Coordinator to join our team.
cond_0262.responsibilities:
Organizes strategies for recruiting study participants and screening study participants for eligibility on the telephone, in the clinic, and other settings as required. Coordinates and oversees patient (study participant) activity as it relates to the conduct of research and clinical trials, serving as a liaison for both patient and Principal Investigator (PI). Serves as primary point of contact for patient to report and triage adverse events and independently conducts informed consent. Arranges necessary tests and procedures in accordance with protocol requirements and reports results to the investigator. Performs clinical laboratory activities as required per protocol and maintains study supplies and equipment. Maintains close communication with study sponsor representatives including but not limited to site initiation, maintenance, and close out of studies. Develops and maintains all required documentation as it relates to the conduct of assigned clinical trials and associated patient care. Completes data entry into sponsor-specific data entry systems and/or supports data coordinator, including query resolution and transcribes information across various internal and external electronic data systems. Conducts daily work and clinical trial activity in accordance with Good Clinical Practice Guidelines. Adapts behavior to the specific patient population, including but not limited to respect for privacy, method of introduction to the patient, adapting explanation of services or procedures to be performed, requesting permissions and communication style. Performs other related duties as assigned.

Act as the primary point of contact for patients to report and triage adverse events, and work with participants through the informed consent process.

cond_0297.intro: This role works alongside departments, staff, patients, and external sponsors to support the conduct of clinical trials. The coordinator helps ensure that all parties understand the requirements of conducting and participating in trials, and shares responsibility for patient care coordination across assigned studies. This position coordinates trials that are more complex and/or greater in number than the associate level.
cond_0297.responsibilities:
Coordinate strategies for recruiting study participants and work with the team to screen participants for eligibility by telephone, in the clinic, and other settings as required.
Serve as a liaison between patients (study participants) and the Principal Investigator (PI), supporting patient activity as it relates to the conduct of research and clinical trials.
Act as the primary point of contact for patients to report and triage adverse events, and work with participants through the informed consent process.
Arrange necessary tests and procedures in accordance with protocol requirements and share results with the investigator.
Support clinical laboratory activities as required per protocol and help maintain study supplies and equipment.
Maintain close communication with study sponsor representatives, including coordination around site initiation, maintenance, and close out of studies.
Develop and maintain all required documentation related to assigned clinical trials and associated patient care.
Complete data entry into sponsor-specific systems and support the data coordinator, including query resolution, and work collaboratively to transcribe information across internal and external electronic data systems.
Carry out daily work and clinical trial activity in accordance with Good Clinical Practice Guidelines.
Adapt approach to the specific patient population, including respect for privacy, method of introduction, explanation of services or procedures, requesting permissions, and communication style.
Perform other related duties as assigned.
The above statements describe the general nature and level of work only. They are not an exhaustive list of all required responsibilities, duties, and skills. Other duties may be added, or this description amended at any time.

cond_0297.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent.
3 Years of relevant research experience in a clinical setting, OR 2 years of relevant research experience in a clinical setting with ACRP or SOCRA certification.
Current Basic Life Support (BLS) certification from the American Heart Association within 60 days of hire. Exceptions will be granted for those in fully remote status.
Knowledge of medical and clinical research terminology and processes.
Working knowledge of ICH guidelines for ethical conduct of research.
Working knowledge of the requirements and regulations associated with the conduct of clinical trials and other related research activity.
Effective verbal and written communication skills and ability to present information clearly and professionally to varying levels of individuals throughout the patient care process.
Ability to travel throughout and between facilities and work a flexible work schedule, including on-call, weekend, and night shifts.
Preferred Requirements
Strong critical thinking skills.
Ability to follow and provide critical feedback on the investigational plan.
Ability to develop study related budgets, contracts, and patient consent documents.
Proficiency in using computers, software, and web-based applications, including working knowledge of [Product name masked].
Strong organizational and time management skills and ability to multi-task, pay close attention to detail, and learn new techniques.

Organizes strategies for recruiting study participants and screening study participants for eligibility on the telephone, in the clinic, and other settings as required. Coordinates and oversees patient (study participant) activity as it relates to the conduct of research and clinical trials, serving as a liaison for both patient and Principal Investigator (PI). Serves as primary point of contact for patient to report and triage adverse events and independently conducts informed consent. Arranges necessary tests and procedures in accordance with protocol requirements and reports results to the investigator. Performs clinical laboratory activities as required per protocol and maintains study supplies and equipment. Maintains close communication with study sponsor representatives including but not limited to site initiation, maintenance, and close out of studies. Develops and maintains all required documentation as it relates to the conduct of assigned clinical trials and associated patient care. Completes data entry into sponsor-specific data entry systems and/or supports data coordinator, including query resolution and transcribes information across various internal and external electronic data systems. Conducts daily work and clinical trial activity in accordance with Good Clinical Practice Guidelines. Adapts behavior to the specific patient population, including but not limited to respect for privacy, method of introduction to the patient, adapting explanation of services or procedures to be performed, requesting permissions and communication style. Performs other related duties as assigned.
The above statements describe the general nature and level of work only. They are not an exhaustive list of all required responsibilities, duties, and skills. Other duties may be added, or this description amended at any time.
Remains knowledgeable on current federal, state, and local laws, accreditation standards or regulatory agency requirements that apply to the assigned area of responsibility and ensures compliance with all such laws, regulations, and standards.
This employer maintains and complies with its Compliance & Privacy Program and Standards of Conduct, including the immediate reporting of any known or suspected unethical or questionable behaviors or conduct; patient/employee safety, patient privacy, and/or other compliance-related concerns.
cond_0316.requirements:
High school diploma or equivalent.
3 Years of relevant research experience in a clinical setting,
OR
2 Years of relevant research experience in a clinical setting with ACRP or SOCRA certification.
Current Basic Life Support (BLS) certification from the American Heart Association within 60 days of hire. Exceptions will be granted for those in fully remote status.
Knowledge of medical and clinical research terminology and processes. Working knowledge of ICH guidelines for ethical conduct of research. Strong critical thinking skills. Ability to follow and provide critical feedback on the investigational plan. Ability to develop study related budgets, contracts, and patient consent documents. Working knowledge of the requirements and regulations associated with the conduct of clinical trials and other related research activity. Proficiency in using computers, software, and web-based applications, including working knowledge of [Product name masked]. Effective verbal and written communication skills and ability to present information clearly and professionally to varying levels of individuals throughout the patient care process. Strong organizational and time management skills and ability to multi-task, pay close attention to detail, and learn new techniques. Ability to travel throughout and between facilities and work a flexible work schedule, including on-call, weekend, and night shifts.
cond_0316.values: We value ambition, achievement, and consistent follow-through. We believe strong outcomes come from maintaining high expectations for the work we do.

Organizes and manages all patient care requirements. Coordinates trials that are more complex and/or a greater number of trials than the associate level.
cond_0415.responsibilities:
Organizes strategies for recruiting study participants and screening study participants for eligibility on the telephone, in the clinic, and other settings as required. Coordinates and oversees patient (study participant) activity as it relates to the conduct of research and clinical trials, serving as a liaison for both patient and Principal Investigator (PI). Serves as primary point of contact for patient to report and triage adverse events and independently conducts informed consent. Arranges necessary tests and procedures in accordance with protocol requirements and reports results to the investigator. Performs clinical laboratory activities as required per protocol and maintains study supplies and equipment. Maintains close communication with study sponsor representatives including but not limited to site initiation, maintenance, and close out of studies. Develops and maintains all required documentation as it relates to the conduct of assigned clinical trials and associated patient care. Completes data entry into sponsor-specific data entry systems and/or supports data coordinator, including query resolution and transcribes information across various internal and external electronic data systems. Conducts daily work and clinical trial activity in accordance with Good Clinical Practice Guidelines. Adapts behavior to the specific patient population, including but not limited to respect for privacy, method of introduction to the patient, adapting explanation of services or procedures to be performed, requesting permissions and communication style. Performs other related duties as assigned.
The above statements describe the general nature and level of work only. They are not an exhaustive list of all required responsibilities, duties, and skills. Other duties may be added, or this description amended at any time.
Remains knowledgeable on current federal, state, and local laws, accreditation standards or regulatory agency requirements that apply to the assigned area of responsibility and ensures compliance with all such laws, regulations, and standards.
This employer maintains and complies with its Compliance & Privacy Program and Standards of Conduct, including the immediate reporting of any known or suspected unethical or questionable behaviors or conduct; patient/employee safety, patient privacy, and/or other compliance-related concerns.
Physical and Environmental Demands
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Medium Work - Exerting 20 to 50 pounds of force occasionally, and/or 10 to 25 pounds of force frequently, and/or greater than negligible up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects. (Constantly: activity or condition exists 2/3 or more of the time) to move objects. Physical demand requirements are in excess of those for Sedentary Work. Even though the weight lifted may be only a negligible amount, a job should be rated Light Work: (1) when it requires walking or standing to a significant degree; or (2) when it requires sitting most of the time but entails pushing and/or pulling of arm or leg controls; and/or (3) when the job requires working at a production rate pace entailing the constant pushing and/or pulling of materials even though the weight of those materials is negligible. NOTE: The constant stress and strain of maintaining a production rate pace, especially in an industrial setting, can be and is physically demanding of a worker even though the amount of force exerted is negligible.
Duties performed routinely require exposure to blood, body fluid and tissue.
The incumbent works in a patient care area; works in an area where patients enter; works directly with patients; and/or works with specimens that could contain communicable diseases. The incumbent has an occupational risk for exposure to all communicable diseases.
Because the incumbent works within a healthcare setting, there may be occupational risk for exposure to hazardous medications or hazardous waste within the environment through receipt, transport, storage, preparation, dispensing, administration, cleaning and/or disposal of contaminated waste. The risk level of exposure may increase depending on the essential job duties of the role.
cond_0415.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent
3 Years of relevant research experience in a clinical setting, OR 2 years of relevant research experience in a clinical setting with ACRP or SOCRA certification
Current Basic Life Support (BLS) certification from the American Heart Association within 60 days of hire. Exceptions will be granted for those in fully remote status
Knowledge of medical and clinical research terminology and processes
Working knowledge of ICH guidelines for ethical conduct of research
Working knowledge of the requirements and regulations associated with the conduct of clinical trials and other related research activity
Strong critical thinking skills
Effective verbal and written communication skills and ability to present information clearly and professionally to varying levels of individuals throughout the patient care process
Strong organizational and time management skills and ability to multi-task, pay close attention to detail, and learn new techniques
Ability to travel throughout and between facilities and work a flexible work schedule, including on-call, weekend, and night shifts
Preferred Requirements
Ability to follow and provide critical feedback on the investigational plan
Ability to develop study related budgets, contracts, and patient consent documents
Proficiency in using computers, software, and web-based applications, including working knowledge of [Product name masked]
cond_0415.values: We value ambition, achievement, and consistent follow-through. We believe strong outcomes come from maintaining high expectations for the work we do.

cond_0459.intro: This role works alongside departments, staff, patients, and external sponsors to support the conduct of clinical trials. The coordinator helps ensure that all parties understand the requirements of conducting and participating in trials, and shares responsibility for patient care coordination across assigned studies. This position coordinates trials that are more complex and/or greater in number than the associate level.
cond_0459.responsibilities:
Coordinate strategies for recruiting study participants and work with the team to screen participants for eligibility by telephone, in the clinic, and other settings as required.
Serve as a liaison between patients (study participants) and the Principal Investigator (PI), supporting patient activity as it relates to the conduct of research and clinical trials.
Act as the primary point of contact for patients to report and triage adverse events, and work with participants through the informed consent process.
Arrange necessary tests and procedures in accordance with protocol requirements and share results with the investigator.
Support clinical laboratory activities as required per protocol and help maintain study supplies and equipment.
Maintain close communication with study sponsor representatives, including coordination around site initiation, maintenance, and close out of studies.
Develop and maintain all required documentation related to assigned clinical trials and associated patient care.
Complete data entry into sponsor-specific systems and support the data coordinator, including query resolution, and work collaboratively to transcribe information across internal and external electronic data systems.
Carry out daily work and clinical trial activity in accordance with Good Clinical Practice Guidelines.
Adapt approach to the specific patient population, including respect for privacy, method of introduction, explanation of services or procedures, requesting permissions, and communication style.
Perform other related duties as assigned.
The above statements describe the general nature and level of work only. They are not an exhaustive list of all required responsibilities, duties, and skills. Other duties may be added, or this description amended at any time.

Physical and Environmental Demands
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Medium Work - Exerting 20 to 50 pounds of force occasionally, and/or 10 to 25 pounds of force frequently, and/or greater than negligible up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects. (Constantly: activity or condition exists 2/3 or more of the time) to move objects. Physical demand requirements are in excess of those for Sedentary Work. Even though the weight lifted may be only a negligible amount, a job should be rated Light Work: (1) when it requires walking or standing to a significant degree; or (2) when it requires sitting most of the time but entails pushing and/or pulling of arm or leg controls; and/or (3) when the job requires working at a production rate pace entailing the constant pushing and/or pulling of materials even though the weight of those materials is negligible. NOTE: The constant stress and strain of maintaining a production rate pace, especially in an industrial setting, can be and is physically demanding of a worker even though the amount of force exerted is negligible.
Duties performed routinely require exposure to blood, body fluid and tissue.
The incumbent works in a patient care area; works in an area where patients enter; works directly with patients; and/or works with specimens that could contain communicable diseases. The incumbent has an occupational risk for exposure to all communicable diseases.
Because the incumbent works within a healthcare setting, there may be occupational risk for exposure to hazardous medications or hazardous waste within the environment through receipt, transport, storage, preparation, dispensing, administration, cleaning and/or disposal of contaminated waste. The risk level of exposure may increase depending on the essential job duties of the role.
cond_0459.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent.
3 Years of relevant research experience in a clinical setting, OR 2 years of relevant research experience in a clinical setting with ACRP or SOCRA certification.
Current Basic Life Support (BLS) certification from the American Heart Association within 60 days of hire. Exceptions will be granted for those in fully remote status.
Knowledge of medical and clinical research terminology and processes.
Working knowledge of ICH guidelines for ethical conduct of research.
Working knowledge of the requirements and regulations associated with the conduct of clinical trials and other related research activity.
Effective verbal and written communication skills and ability to present information clearly and professionally to varying levels of individuals throughout the patient care process.
Ability to travel throughout and between facilities and work a flexible work schedule, including on-call, weekend, and night shifts.
Preferred Requirements
Strong critical thinking skills.
Ability to follow and provide critical feedback on the investigational plan.
Ability to develop study related budgets, contracts, and patient consent documents.
Proficiency in using computers, software, and web-based applications, including working knowledge of [Product name masked].
Strong organizational and time management skills and ability to multi-task, pay close attention to detail, and learn new techniques.

Serve as a liaison between patients (study participants) and the Principal Investigator (PI), supporting patient activity as it relates to the conduct of research and clinical trials.
Act as the primary point of contact for patients to report and triage adverse events, and work with participants through the informed consent process.
Arrange necessary tests and procedures in accordance with protocol requirements and share results with the investigator.
Support clinical laboratory activities as required per protocol and help maintain study supplies and equipment.
Maintain close communication with study sponsor representatives, including coordination around site initiation, maintenance, and close out of studies.
Develop and maintain all required documentation related to assigned clinical trials and associated patient care.
Complete data entry into sponsor-specific systems and support the data coordinator, including query resolution, and work collaboratively to transcribe information across internal and external electronic data systems.
Carry out daily work and clinical trial activity in accordance with Good Clinical Practice Guidelines.
Adapt approach to the specific patient population, including respect for privacy, method of introduction, explanation of services or procedures, requesting permissions, and communication style.
Perform other related duties as assigned.

cond_0602.intro: This role owns all activities related to the conduct of clinical trials. You will lead communication with external funding agencies and sponsors, other departments, departmental staff, and patients to ensure requirements for conducting and participating in clinical trials are met. You will direct all patient care requirements and manage trials that are more complex and/or greater in number than the associate level.
cond_0602.responsibilities:
Determine and execute strategies for recruiting study participants and screening them for eligibility on the telephone, in the clinic, and other settings as required.
Lead and oversee patient (study participant) activity as it relates to the conduct of research and clinical trials, serving as a liaison for both patient and Principal Investigator (PI).
Serve as primary point of contact for patients to report and triage adverse events and independently conduct informed consent.
Arrange necessary tests and procedures in accordance with protocol requirements and report results to the investigator.
Perform clinical laboratory activities as required per protocol and maintain study supplies and equipment.
Direct close communication with study sponsor representatives including but not limited to site initiation, maintenance, and close out of studies.
Develop and maintain all required documentation as it relates to the conduct of assigned clinical trials and associated patient care.
Execute data entry into sponsor-specific data entry systems and/or direct data coordinator support, including query resolution, and transcribe information across various internal and external electronic data systems.
Conduct daily work and clinical trial activity in accordance with Good Clinical Practice Guidelines.
Adapt behavior to the specific patient population, including but not limited to respect for privacy, method of introduction to the patient, adapting explanation of services or procedures to be performed, requesting permissions and communication style.
Perform other related duties as assigned.
The above statements describe the general nature and level of work only. They are not an exhaustive list of all required responsibilities, duties, and skills. Other duties may be added, or this description amended at any time.

cond_0602.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent.
3 Years of relevant research experience in a clinical setting, OR 2 years of relevant research experience in a clinical setting with ACRP or SOCRA certification.
Current Basic Life Support (BLS) certification from the American Heart Association within 60 days of hire. Exceptions will be granted for those in fully remote status.
Knowledge of medical and clinical research terminology and processes.
Working knowledge of ICH guidelines for ethical conduct of research.
Working knowledge of the requirements and regulations associated with the conduct of clinical trials and other related research activity.
Effective verbal and written communication skills and ability to present information clearly and professionally to varying levels of individuals throughout the patient care process.
Ability to travel throughout and between facilities and work a flexible work schedule, including on-call, weekend, and night shifts.
Preferred Requirements
Strong critical thinking skills.
Ability to follow and provide critical feedback on the investigational plan.
Ability to develop study related budgets, contracts, and patient consent documents.
Proficiency in using computers, software, and web-based applications, including working knowledge of [Product name masked].
Strong organizational and time management skills and ability to multi-task, pay close attention to detail, and learn new techniques.

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Medium Work - Exerting 20 to 50 pounds of force occasionally, and/or 10 to 25 pounds of force frequently, and/or greater than negligible up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects. (Constantly: activity or condition exists 2/3 or more of the time) to move objects. Physical demand requirements are in excess of those for Sedentary Work. Even though the weight lifted may be only a negligible amount, a job should be rated Light Work: (1) when it requires walking or standing to a significant degree; or (2) when it requires sitting most of the time but entails pushing and/or pulling of arm or leg controls; and/or (3) when the job requires working at a production rate pace entailing the constant pushing and/or pulling of materials even though the weight of those materials is negligible. NOTE: The constant stress and strain of maintaining a production rate pace, especially in an industrial setting, can be and is physically demanding of a worker even though the amount of force exerted is negligible.
Duties performed routinely require exposure to blood, body fluid and tissue.
The incumbent works in a patient care area; works in an area where patients enter; works directly with patients; and/or works with specimens that could contain communicable diseases. The incumbent has an occupational risk for exposure to all communicable diseases.
Because the incumbent works within a healthcare setting, there may be occupational risk for exposure to hazardous medications or hazardous waste within the environment through receipt, transport, storage, preparation, dispensing, administration, cleaning and/or disposal of contaminated waste. The incumbent works in a patient care area; works in an area where patients enter; works directly with patients; and/or works with specimens that could contain communicable diseases. The incumbent has an occupational risk for exposure to all communicable diseases.
